# Pandamonium v1.0.74

This hotfix restores reliable native Entertainment playback for large proxied HLS manifests. It keeps the existing SSRF, DNS-rebinding, redirect, ownership, expiry, range, size, header, content-type, and no-store protections intact. Rollback remains signed v1.0.73 and the updater's retained pre-update snapshot.

## MAD-974 — Entertainment: make proxied HLS playback start reliably

### Problem

Rewriting a 309-segment HLS manifest performed DNS-backed public-address validation once per media URI. The response took about 25 seconds, exceeding hls.js's 10-second manifest timeout. Its retry minted another full token set, evicted the original manifest token from the bounded store, and ended in a 404 instead of starting playback.

### Implementation

Manifest rewriting now reuses an unexpired token for the same owner, URL, and required headers. Token creation performs only bounded URL syntax validation; every outbound fetch still performs full public-address validation and uses the existing pinned transport before connecting.

### Product value and UI visibility

Anime and movie HLS streams can begin in the native Entertainment player without waiting on hundreds of redundant DNS lookups or losing the root manifest token during a retry. No visual or interaction design changed.

### Verification

A failure-first 309-segment regression reproduced the slow rewrite and token eviction. Focused Entertainment and SSRF/pinning coverage passed 19 checks, the full Python suite passed 6,527 tests with five skips, and the full Chromium suite passed all 190 tests. Protected PR CI passed Python, browser, syntax, dependency, secret, workflow, container, and image gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, schema, environment variable, authentication, proxy contract, or stored-data change was introduced. The token store remains bounded at 512 entries and tokens retain their existing ownership and expiry rules.
